clue.text: God, nearly accepting bribe, returned initial payment

indicators.note: accepting means the shortened god takes the bribe inside it
nearly means the word for god loses its final letter

parts.note: a god is a deity

indicators.note: returned means the word for a bribe is read backwards

parts.note: a sop is a small bribe or appeasing gift

explanation.surface: A deity takes a bribe and hands back a first instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'God, nearly' makes it read as an exclamation, but 'nearly' trims the god and 'returned' belongs to the bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a part-payment made up front to secure a purchase.

clue.text: See 2
Mess with pawn to knock down, getting level on board

parts.note: poo is a childish word for excrement, a mess
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
to deck someone is to knock them down

explanation.surface: Someone fouls a chessboard and knocks a pawn over while trying to level the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' sounds like chess, which the pawn encourages, but it means aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A poop deck is a raised floor at the stern of a ship, one storey of the vessel.

clue.text: "Mirror" has problem carrying page with cryptic clue

indicators.note: carrying means the word for a problem holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters of clue are muddled

explanation.surface: A crossword-style teaser about a mirror, set as a sum with a cryptic clue on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic clue' looks like self-reference by the setter; it is the anagram signal plus its fodder, placed with the page letter inside the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculum is Latin for a looking-glass, and the word also names a mirror of polished metal in a telescope.

clue.text: Unfortunate yobbo

definitions.meaning: a yobbo is a British slang word for a rough, aggressive young man, a thug

explanation.definitionFit: Tough means unlucky in 'tough luck', and as a noun a tough is a hooligan or thug.

clue.text: Incarnation of Vishnu in the hearts of Dave, Kate and Gary

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the middle pair of each name is taken

explanation.surface: A Hindu god appears to live in the affections of three ordinary friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Each name gives its middle two letters: AV, AT, AR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism an avatar is a god's descent to earth in bodily form, Krishna and Rama being Vishnu's best known.

clue.text: As opposed to being oversusceptible in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the long word is taken, the run sitting within it

explanation.surface: Someone is described as contrary because they are a little too thin-skinned.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside overSUSceptible: o-VERSUS-ceptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is the Latin preposition meaning against, set in opposition to.

clue.text: Liberated, topless and hot, embraced by one who pulls hippie type

indicators.note: embraced by means the other letters are held inside the puller

parts.note: a tugger is one who tugs or pulls

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: liberated means set free
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A freed, half-naked and steamy person is cuddled by someone trying to pull them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who pulls' suggests a seducer, but it is literal: someone who tugs, opened up to take the freed, topless letters and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-hugger is a mocking name for an environmentalist, seen as a hippie in spirit.

clue.text: A more tired, knackered measurer of energy levels

indicators.note: knackered, British slang for worn out or broken, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone even more worn out is themselves an exhausted gauge of how much energy they have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tired' and 'knackered' both suggest fatigue, but one is fodder and the other the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiometer is an instrument that measures the intensity of radiant energy.

clue.text: Short of success, ruling tobaccoes out

definitions.meaning: nearly, but not quite, achieving something: the phrase said after a near miss
read whimsically, saying there is to be ..., banning tobacco

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the catchphrase literally: the prize cigar is being refused.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said of an attempt that came near to succeeding but fell short, from fairground prizes of cigars.

clue.text: Day before check mate

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, a day
to check something is to stop or end it

explanation.surface: A chess move: a day's play leads to check and then mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check mate' looks like chess, but 'check' is END and 'mate' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is an informal word for a pal or companion.

clue.text: Sound system required way before getting old

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A hi-fi had to be bought on the road before it became outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a hi-fi system that plays sound through two channels.

clue.text: Predator's call reported, that is to say, to court

indicators.note: reported means the words are as heard spoken, not as spelt

parts.words: that is to say, to court
parts.note: to wit is an old phrase meaning that is to say, namely; to woo is to court someone romantically

explanation.surface: An announcement that a hunter's cry has been heard, with legal phrasing about going to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' tempts a law reading, but it is courtship.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the conventional rendering of the hoot of an owl, a nocturnal bird of prey.

clue.text: Cleans round joint with fifty strokes

indicators.note: round means the cleaning word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to wash something is to clean it
the hip is a joint of the body
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone rubbing down a sore joint is given fifty lashes as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashes from a whip are strokes delivered as punishment.

clue.text: Paul's 10 black, held by white, can't be touched

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so 'Paul's' is 'Paul is', from his own mouth I'm
10 across is friend, and a pal is a friend

indicators.note: held by means the letter for black is put inside the word for white

parts.note: pale means whitish, lacking colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The setter's buddy, black and held by a white man, is beyond reach.
explanation.walkthrough: PA(B)LE holds B; the setter speaking for himself gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalpable means not able to be felt or touched, intangible.

clue.text: Cheats stink, loathsome people

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
buggers is a British vulgar term for contemptible people

explanation.surface: A complaint that some odious people both deceive and smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbuggers are those who practise humbug, deceivers or frauds.

clue.text: Oz girl had cat, dog's dinner for Oz croc!

indicators.note: a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Australian girl's cat became food for a crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is crossword shorthand for Australia; the anagram uses every letter of 'Oz girl had cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gotcha lizard is Australian slang, popularised by Crocodile Dundee, for a crocodile.

clue.text: Encourage happiness, though left out

indicators.note: out means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: glee is great happiness

explanation.surface: Someone urges joy on a group, though one member is excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is used in 'gee up', urging a horse or person on.

clue.text: Irregular, short owner of pointy ears eating vegetable mum discarded

indicators.note: eating means the shortened name takes the vegetable inside it
short means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Mr Spock is the pointy-eared Vulcan of Star Trek

indicators.note: discarded means the word for mum is thrown out

parts.note: a radish is a root vegetable
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A pointy-eared character is uneven in eating a vegetable his mother threw away.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals or only here and there.

clue.text: Fruit cut, going to seed

indicators.note: cut means the fruit is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Sliced fruit is turning to seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to seed' looks like a phrase about decay, but 'going to' links and 'seed' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is the round seed of a leguminous plant, found in a pod.

clue.text: Doctor in spat about present environment

indicators.note: in means the doctor goes inside the reworked letters
about means the letters of spat are moved around

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A doctor in a quarrel worries about the current setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SPAT into ATSP, which holds MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere means the surrounding air or mood of a place, its environment.

clue.text: See 16
Gripping success, dreadful ham with repeat performances here

indicators.note: gripping means the scrambled letters hold the word for success
dreadful means very bad, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A gripping success with a dreadful hammy actor doing repeat performances.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled ham-and-repeat letters split after their third letter to grip the success word; 'here' makes the definition a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an open circular venue where shows and contests are staged.

clue.text: Being possibly two-faced, four-eyed, spotty and legless makes a boy upset

definitions.text: Being possibly two-faced, four-eyed, spotty and legless

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the name is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Insults about a boy's looks and drunkenness upset him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as playground abuse; 'legless' (British for very drunk) here just means without legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An extraterrestrial might be imagined with any odd features, so a creature of two faces and four eyes could be one.

clue.text: Family's regal tragedy

parts.note: a play by Shakespeare in which a monarch's division of his realm among his daughters ends in ruin

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy centres on an old British ruler and the betrayal by his daughters.

clue.text: See 24
Shed almost caught in roll, part of wheel

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a hut is a shed

indicators.note: in means the cricket letter goes inside the roll

parts.note: a bap is a soft British bread roll
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Bread rolls stored in a shed, with a cap for a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hubcap is the metal cover over the centre of a car wheel.

clue.text: Tube where drink absorbs last of bird seed

indicators.note: absorbs means the drink takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: wine is a drink

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of bird is taken

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A bird's feeder, where a drink soaks up the last of the seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the trachea, the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Firm set about woman when leaderless

indicators.note: about means the letters of set are moved around
leaderless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A company sets out on behalf of a woman without a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SET into STE; LADY loses its head to give ADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means firm and stable, not shaking.

clue.text: See 9
